messages:
jena: Heads-up — we're seeing a sustained read/write latency spike on scratchfs mounts on a subset of GPU nodes in us-west-2. Several GPU pods got OOM-killed after long stalls.
samir: Which instance family and how many nodes affected?
jena: Mostly c6g->no, sorry, g4dn.* and a couple of p4d-simulated test nodes. Start count ~6 nodes.
maggie: Seeing correlating alerts: iowait > 70% and kernel reports of high read amplification.
ben: I pulled a quick iostat and dmesg from node-gpu-07: 
```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   rrqm/s   wrqm/s  r_await  w_await svctm  %util
sda              430.0   20.1    0.00     0.00    10.20    1.30   0.80  99.9
```
And dmesg has repeated lines: 
```
blk_update_request: I/O error, dev sda, sector 123456
scsi host0: reset routine succeeded for target 0
```
kai: That looks like high queue depth + background scrub activity. Any recent kernel or agent changes?
jena: We deployed a storage agent change yesterday that enabled more aggressive 'scrub-and-reclaim' on scratchfs. Patch: increase scrub concurrency to 8.
samir: That might explain read amplification. Scrub is scanning small random blocks, causing a lot of small reads while GPUs do large sequential reads.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1934 (storage-high-iops-us-west-2)
maggie: Short-term mitigation candidates: 1) throttle scrub concurrency to 1 2) pin scrub to off-peak maintenance window 3) enable IO cgroup limits for kube pods touching /scratch
ben: I can push a change to reduce concurrency and add a node-local flag to exclude g4dn/P4 instance families.
kai: Also consider enabling blk-mq timeouts and setting elevator to fq to avoid starvation.
jena: Agreed. Let's try throttling first. ben, do you want to run a canary on node-gpu-07?
ben: On it. Pushing: /etc/scratchfs/scrub.conf diff: 
```
-concurrency = 8
+concurrency = 1
+exclude_families = ["g4dn","p4d"]
```
Deploying to node-gpu-07 now.
(2m later)
ben: Canary done. iostat shows util down to 35% and r_await dropped to 1.8ms on node-gpu-07.
maggie: Nice. Any sign of corruption from scrub logs?
jena: Scrub logs show some recoverable read errors but no unrecoverable sectors yet. We should run a deeper nvme SMART check during maintenance.
samir: Action items: 
- ben to roll scrub concurrency change to remaining impacted nodes (6) with exclusion flag (ETA 30m)
- kai to add IO cgroup rule to kubelet profile for scratch mounts (ETA 2h)
- maggie to schedule SMART checks and compile list of nodes with increased read error counts (ETA 4h)
- jena to update runbook to include scrub throttling as a mitigation
infra-bot: note: rolling deploy will trigger node disruption; mark as maintenance in console.
ben: Rolling now. Will do 2 nodes at a time and watch eviction rate.
jena: Cost/ops note — disabling aggressive scrub raises risk of delayed cleanup and higher long-term wear; track cumulative errors and plan a slower background defrag in off-hours.
kai: Also open question: is scratchfs default policy too aggressive for instances with consumer-grade NVMe firmware? We might need family-specific defaults.
maggie: I'll start a doc for 'scratchfs tuning by instance family' and add historical telemetry.
samir: For postmortem: capture metrics for iops/latency pre/post, scrub throughput, eviction counts, and any kernel updates.
jena: Thanks team. If latency resurfaces after the roll, re-open incident. For now, throttling looks to have stabilized the fleet. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident INC-2026-1934 marked: mitigated
